To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

small gold nanoparticles induce two processes in the DNA cholesterics: (i) the reorganization of the cholesteric spatial structure to the nematic one, and (ii) the formation of linear ensembles of gold nanoparticles in “free space” of quasinematic liquid-crystallinity layers.

small-size gold nanoparticles (2 nm) are capable of forming ensembles consisting of nanoparticles and linear chains of gold nanoparticles in liquid-crystallines formed by DNA molecules, and these ensembles are located between the DNA molecules in the quasinemetic layers of liquid-crystal particles.

gold nanoparticles induce a reorganization of the DNA liquid-crystelline dispersion particles from cholesteric to nematic phase, they can form linear clusters of gold particles, and the formation of these clusters is likely due to the presence of DNA molecules in the quasinematics layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of gold nanoparticles of small size (2 nm) on the properties of DNA particles of cholesterol liquid-crystallines dispersions.

the development of a method to study the interaction of gold nanoparticles with DNA molecules, and the formation of linear aggregates of gold nanoparticles, which can be used as nanomaterials in the development of nanobiotechnologies and nanomedicine.
the formation of ensembled consisting of gold nanoparticles in DNA liquid-crystalls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gold nanoparticles, which have a size of about 2 nm, are not able to form clusters of gold nanoparticles.
the presence of linear clusters of nanoparticles in the quasinematically structured liquid-crystallin particles of DNA can be considered as a new type of nanomaterial.

the formation of gold nanoparticles ensembles is the result of the interplay of several factors, such as the presence of DNA molecules, their orientation and ordering in the liquid-crystallized particles, and the size of the particles of gold nanoparticles, and their surface properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of gold nanoparticles with small sizes in the study of the properties of liquid-crystALLINE dispersions formed by DNA molecules is a new and very promising direction of scientific research.
the use of gold nanoparticles in DNA liquid-crystALLINE dispersions can be a promising approach for the design of new materials and devices for nanoelectronics and nanobiotechnologies.
gold nanoparticles are not toxic for DNA molecules and do not affect the spatial cholesterol structure of DNA liquid-crystal particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of gold nanoparticles as contrast agents in the study of DNA structures in living cells can lead to erroneous conclusions.
the formation of clusters of gold nanoparticles depends on the size of nanoparticles and the concentration of DNA in the liquid-crystallizing system.
gold nanoparticles with a size of ∼2 nm can be used as an effective tool for studying the properties of cholesterics formed by DNA molecules.
